"""A question/negation-sensitive auxiliary-word predictor.

The biggest response is on `do` in `what/how/why ... do` questions.
Commands and `don't` are positive too; infinitival/modal `do` is almost quiet.
Smaller rules cover related auxiliaries, French `pas`, and a few short phrases.
Strengths are estimated from training activations, not a model or token-ID table.
Spelling variants of do/don't and compound oneOf/anyOf/allOf forms have explicit rules.
Only the last 140 characters are kept, resetting at document boundaries.
"""
import re
import wordnet

READS = ()
WH = {'what', 'how', 'why', 'where', 'when', 'who', 'which'}
SUBJECTS = {'i', 'you', 'he', 'she', 'it', 'we', 'they', 'there'}
MODALS = {'can', 'could', 'would', 'should', 'will', 'shall', 'may', 'might', 'must'}
BLOCK = SUBJECTS | MODALS | {
    'to', 'is', 'are', 'was', 'were', 'be', 'am',
    'has', 'have', 'had', 'does', 'did', 'do',
}
COMMAND_LINKS = {'and', 'but', 'or', 'so', 'then', 'please', 'never'}
PUNCTUATION_END = re.compile(r'[,;:.!?"\n]\s*$')


def question_cue(tail):
    """Recognize a recent wh-word or a short what/how question phrase.

    Intervening subjects/verbs block the cue. Other wh-words only count
    directly, and relative `who/which/when` clauses are mostly excluded.
    """
    clause = re.split(r'[.!?;\n]', tail)[-1]
    clause = re.sub(r'(?<=[a-z])(?=[A-Z])', ' ', clause)
    clause = re.sub(r'(?<=[A-Z])(?=[A-Z][a-z])', ' ', clause)
    matches = list(re.finditer(r'[A-Za-z]+', clause))[-8:]
    words = [m.group().lower() for m in matches]
    for i in range(len(words) - 1, -1, -1):
        q, rest = words[i], words[i + 1:]
        if q not in WH:
            continue
        if rest and q not in {'what', 'how'}: return ''
        if any(w in BLOCK for w in rest): return ''
        if q in {'who', 'which'} and not matches[i].group()[0].isupper():
            return ''
        if q in {'who', 'which', 'when'}:
            lead = clause[:matches[i].start()].strip(' \t,\"\'([{')
            if lead and not matches[i].group()[0].isupper(): return ''
        if q == 'how' and rest and not (
            {'adjective', 'adverb'} & wordnet.parts_of_speech(rest[0])
        ) and rest[0] not in {
            'many', 'much', 'long', 'often', 'far', 'exactly', 'else',
            'well', 'on', 'then', 'ever',
        }:
            return ''
        if (q == 'what' and rest and rest[0] == 'the'
                and not {'hell', 'fuck'}.intersection(rest)):
            return ''
        return 'phrase' if rest else q
    return ''


def activation(token, tail):
    s = token.strip()
    word = s.lower()
    if token == 'Of':
        head = re.search(r'(one|any|all)$', tail, re.I)
        if head: return {'one': -4.8, 'any': -5.5, 'all': -2.5}[head[0].lower()]
    if token in {'_of', '-of'} and re.search(r'one$', tail, re.I):
        return -2.4 if token == '_of' else -3.5
    if s == 't' and re.search(r"don(?:\\)?['’]$", tail, re.I): return 3.0
    if token == 'on' and re.search(r'(?:^|[^A-Za-z])[dD]$', tail): return 3.5
    if word not in {
        'do', 'don', 'dont', 'are', 'have', 'am', 'were', 'art',
        'not', 'pas', 'about', 'a', 'of',
        "'t", '’t',
    }:
        return 2.2 if re.fullmatch(r'[^a-z]*do', word) else 0.001
    words = re.findall(r'[a-z]+', tail.lower())[-9:]
    prev = words[-1] if words else ''
    q = question_cue(tail)

    inverted = prev in {'nor', 'neither'} or words[-2:] == ['not', 'only']
    if word in {'do', 'are', 'have', 'am', 'were', 'art'} and inverted:
        return {'do': 4.7, 'are': 2.5, 'have': 2.5,
                'am': 2.0, 'were': 1.0, 'art': 1.0}[word]

    if word == 'don': return 3.5 if q else 0.1
    if word == 'do':
        if s == 'DO': return 0.8
        if token == 'do' and tail[-1:].isalpha():
            return 0.65                       # A suffix inside a word.
        if token == 'do' and tail[-1:] and not tail[-1:].isspace():
            return 2.5                        # Quoted/code word boundary.
        if q:
            return {'what': 10.2, 'how': 9.4, 'why': 7.7,
                    'where': 6.5, 'when': 6.5, 'who': 7.7,
                    'which': 7.0, 'phrase': 6.8}[q]
        if s == 'Do': return 3.5
        adverb = prev in {'only', 'really', 'actually', 'also', 'ever',
                          'always', 'possibly'}
        if prev in MODALS | {'to'} or (
            adverb and len(words) > 1 and words[-2] in MODALS | {'to'}
        ):
            return -0.065
        if prev in SUBJECTS: return 0.5
        if prev in COMMAND_LINKS: return 2.7
        if re.search(r'(?:/[*]|//|function)\s*$', tail): return 2.7
        if prev in {'really', 'indeed'}: return 1.3
        if not tail.strip() or tail.endswith('\n'): return 2.2
        if re.search(r'[,;:.!?"\]\)]\s*$', tail): return 2.9
        return 0.7

    if word in {"'t", '’t'}:
        if prev != 'don': return 0.14
        before = tail[:tail.lower().rfind('don')]
        if question_cue(before): return 6.6
        if tail.rstrip().endswith('Don'): return 3.5
        earlier = re.findall(r'[a-z]+', before.lower())
        subject = earlier[-1] if earlier else ''
        if subject == 'i': return 2.05
        if subject in {'you', 'we', 'they'}: return 1.0
        if not before.strip() or subject in COMMAND_LINKS or (
            PUNCTUATION_END.search(before)
        ):
            return 3.0
        return 1.05
    if word == 'dont': return 0.7

    if word == 'were': return 1.8 if q else -0.05
    if word == 'art': return 1.0 if prev == 'thou' else 0.001
    if word in {'are', 'have', 'am'}:
        if word == 'am' and s != 'am': return 0.05
        if q:
            if q == 'phrase': return {'are': 2.0, 'have': 1.9, 'am': 3.0}[word]
            return {'are': 3.0, 'have': 5.5, 'am': 4.0}[word]
        if s[0].isupper(): return {'are': 2.1, 'have': 2.1, 'am': 0.05}[word]
        if PUNCTUATION_END.search(tail): return 1.8 if word == 'are' else 1.1
        if prev in COMMAND_LINKS: return 0.6 if word == 'are' else 0.8
        if word == 'are':
            if prev == 'here': return 0.65
            if tail.rstrip().endswith('There'): return -0.53
            return 0.4 if prev == 'and' else 0.0
        return 0.04

        before = tail[:tail.lower().rfind('do')].rstrip()
        if tail.rstrip().endswith('Do') or PUNCTUATION_END.search(before):
            return 1.9
        subject = re.findall(r'[a-z]+', before.lower())

        return 1.5 if p == 'i' or p in COMMAND_LINKS else 0.5
    if s == 'pas': return 1.15
    if s == 'about': return 1.1 if prev in {'how', 'what'} else -0.05
    if s == 'a':

        if prev in {'are','were'} and 'there' in words[-4:]: return -1.2
    if s == 'of':
        if prev == 'one': return -0.12
        if q and prev in {'kind', 'type', 'sort', 'form', 'much', 'many'}:

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    tail = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]

   negative when it is a word (about -0.2), moderately negative for other symbols or

than late-alphabet variables. Fused punctuation is discounted. Chinese numeral
labels and repeated middle-dot decorations have their own positive pulses.
Only a bounded text suffix is kept, reset at document boundaries.
"""
import re

READS = ()
VALUES = {
    'line_number_first': 1.17,
    'line_number_small': 3.14,
    'line_number_tens': 2.25,
    'line_number_long': 1.04,
    'line_letter_first': 1.62,
    'line_letter_lower': 1.43,
    'line_letter_early': 4.52,
    'line_letter_upper': 3.08,
    'line_roman': 3.74,
    'line_han': 3.77,
    'inline_number': 0.31,
    'inline_letter_first': 0.22,
    'inline_letter_early': 1.06,
    'inline_roman': 0.35,
    'paren_number': 0.47,
    'paren_letter_first': 0.77,
    'paren_letter_early': 2.04,
    'paren_roman': 1.86,
    'middle_dots': 2.05,
}
HAN_NUMBERS = frozenset('零〇一二三四五六七八九十百千万壹贰叁肆伍陆柒捌玖拾')
LABEL = re.compile(r'([^\W_]+)$')
ROMAN = re.compile(
    r'M{0,3}(CM|CD|D?C{0,3})(XC|XL|L?X{0,3})(IX|IV|V?I{0,3})$'
)

AFTER_SENTENCE_SCALE = 0.3


def rule(token, text):
    if len(token) >= 2 and set(token) == {'·'}:
        return 'middle_dots', 1.0
    if not token or token[0] not in '.)．）、：:],-ºª条章':
        return '', 0.0
    mark = token[0]
    text = text.replace('\\n', '\n').replace('<|endoftext|>', '\n')
    text = text.replace('\r', '\n').rstrip(' \t')
    if not text or not text[-1].isalnum():
        return '', 0.0
    label = LABEL.search(text)[0]
    before = text[:-len(label)]
    if label.isdecimal():
        n = int(label) if len(label) < 7 else 1000000
        kind = 'number'
    elif label[-1] in HAN_NUMBERS and (
            all(c in HAN_NUMBERS for c in label) or mark in '：条章'):
        kind = 'han'
    elif len(label) > 1 and ROMAN.fullmatch(label.upper()):
        kind = 'roman'
    elif len(label) == 1 and label.isalpha():
        kind = 'letter_first' if label.lower() == 'a' else (
            'letter_upper' if label.isupper() else 'letter_lower')
    else:
        return '', 0.0
    line = before.rsplit('\n', 1)[-1]
    line_start = all(c.isspace() or c in '*#->([（【•◦▪●□☐' for c in line)
    opened = before.endswith(('(', '（', '[', '【'))
    spaced_open = opened and (len(before) == 1 or before[-2].isspace())
    spaced = bool(before[-1:].isspace())
    sentence_end = before.rstrip().rstrip('([（【').rstrip()
    after_sentence = sentence_end.endswith(('.', ':', ';', '!', '?', '。', '：'))
    if (len(sentence_end) > 1 and sentence_end[-1:] == '.'
            and sentence_end[-2].isdigit()):
        after_sentence = False  # not the dot inside a decimal or version number
    if not line_start and not (spaced or spaced_open):
        return '', 0.0
    if not line_start and kind == 'letter_lower' and label in 'xyz':
        return '', 0.0  # common algebraic variables rather than list letters
    if kind == 'letter_lower' and label in 'bcdefgh':
        kind = 'letter_early'
    at_start = line_start or after_sentence
    place = 'line' if at_start else 'paren' if spaced_open else 'inline'
    if at_start and kind == 'number':
        kind += '_first' if n == 1 else '_small' if n < 10 else (
            '_tens' if n < 100 else '_long')
    key = place + '_' + kind
    scale = AFTER_SENTENCE_SCALE if after_sentence and not line_start else 1.0
    if kind == 'number' and not at_start:
        scale *= 0.4 if n == 1 else 1.0 if n < 10 else 0.6
    if mark in ':：':
        scale *= 0.25 if mark == ':' else 0.65
    elif mark in ',-':
        scale *= 0.2 if at_start else 0.0
    elif mark == ']':
        scale *= 0.25
    if len(token) > 1:
        scale *= 0.07 if token[1:].isspace() else (
            0.8 if token in ('.)', ').') else 0.3)
    return key, scale


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    tail = b'' if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    key, scale = rule(token, tail.decode('utf-8', errors='replace'))
    value = 0.003 + scale * VALUES.get(key, 0.0)
    tail = (tail + prefix.token_bytes[-1])[-768:]
    return (doc, tail), float(value)

"""List-marker punctuation: fires on the '.' or ')' that closes a list label at line start.

Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2108 responds to the punctuation that closes a list marker
at the start of a line: "2." or "13." or "3)" after a line break, or "b." / "c)" as a letter
marker. Its activation is large (about 2.5 to 3) for list numbers 2 to 9 and for letters, a
little smaller for two-digit numbers, weaker for "1." (often the first item of a list), and
zero for "0.". A digit closed by '.' or ')' in the middle of a line ("...others. 3.") gives a
weak response. Inline panel letters such as "(C)" inside a sentence are not captured.

The rule looks only at the last few tokens, so it needs no carried state.
"""

READS = ()

# Punctuation that closes a label.
CLOSERS = {".", ")", ":", "]", "、", "）"}


def _label_and_before(toks):
    """Walk back from the newest token over the marker: a run of up to three digit tokens,
    or one short alphanumeric token (a letter, roman numeral or '(b'). Returns the label
    length, the marker's text, and the token that precedes it."""
    j = len(toks) - 2
    digits = 0
    while j >= 0 and len(toks[j]) == 1 and toks[j].isdigit() and digits < 3:
        j -= 1
        digits += 1
    if digits:
        label = "".join(toks[j + 1 : len(toks) - 1])
        return label, "digit", toks[j] if j >= 0 else ""
    word = toks[-2].lstrip("(")
    if 1 <= len(word) <= 3 and word.isalnum():
        return word, "letter", toks[-3] if len(toks) >= 3 else ""
    return "", "", ""


def activation(toks):
    """Predicted activation at the newest token of `toks` (a list of token strings)."""
    if len(toks) < 3 or toks[-1] not in CLOSERS:
        return 0.0
    label, kind, before = _label_and_before(toks)
    if not kind:
        return 0.0
    line_start = "\n" in before or before == ""
    if not line_start:
        # a digit closed by '.' or ')' in the middle of a line
        return 0.5 if (kind == "digit" and toks[-1] in (".", ")")) else 0.0
    if kind == "letter":
        return 2.8  # "a." / "b)" starting a line
    if label == "0":
        return 0.0
    if label == "1":
        return 1.1  # the first item of a list is weaker
    return 3.0 if len(label) == 1 else 2.4  # "2." ... "9.", then "10." ... "13."


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    toks = list(prefix.token_strings[-5:])
    return carry, float(activation(toks))

"""Oil-spelling detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2109 (layer 1, MLP down projection).

The component fires on the token that completes the spelling "oil", or a word built on it:
  - whole words for oil and its rhymes: "oil", "coil", "soil", "boil", "foil", "toil",
    "recoil", "broil", "oiled", "boiling", ...; strongest on "oil" and "coil";
  - the "il" piece that the tokenizer splits off after an "o": "co|il", "AMSO|IL",
    "bro|il", "o|iled", "o|ils";
  - the German and Japanese words for oil ("Öl", "イル" in オイル, "油");
  - the "2" of "CO2" after "CO".
It stays near zero on everything else, including one-token words that merely contain
"oil" ("turmoil") and "il" pieces after other letters ("Conse|il").

The values are typical average activations for each case, not per-token fits. Predictions
are 0 everywhere else; the component's small diffuse background is not modelled.
"""

OIL_WORDS = {
    "oil", "oils", "coil", "coils", "soil", "soils", "boil", "boils", "foil", "foils",
    "toil", "spoil", "recoil", "broil", "roil", "oily", "oiled", "boiled", "coiled",
    "soiled", "oiling", "boiling", "coiling", "boiler", "broiler",
}
OIL_FOREIGN = {"öl", "イル", "油", "オイル"}

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: the lowercased text of the current document so far (last 12 characters).
    tail = carry or ""
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    if len(docs) > 1 and docs[-1] != docs[-2]:
        tail = ""  # a new document starts: forget the previous text
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    before = tail
    tail = (tail + token.lower())[-12:]

    if word in OIL_WORDS or word in OIL_FOREIGN:
        return tail, 5.5
    if word == "2" and before.endswith("co"):
        return tail, 4.0  # the 2 of CO2
    if word.startswith("il") and before.endswith("o") and word.isascii():
        return tail, 6.0  # the "il" of "oil" split across tokens: co|il, bro|iled
    return tail, 0.0

"""A Latin-spelling reach / r-vowel-ch approximation.

Whole reach tokens are strong, but reachable and outreach have their own
strengths. Wordpieces completing r-vowel-ch are also strong, especially
reich and sprich/sprech-like clusters. Within-token matches require a short
continuation piece. This is about spelling and
token boundaries, not a general meaning of reaching. A small negative signal
marks each and re-in/re-co continuations. Two header conventions are handled
separately: Title: after end-of-text, and the reply label Re:.
The ordinary spelling rules keep five preceding characters and reset at each
document boundary; the Title: rule checks the preceding two tokens.
"""
import re
READS = ()
VOWELS = 'aeiouyäöü'
RHOTIC = re.compile(r'r([' + VOWELS + r']{1,3})(ch|ck|k|p)')
ROOT = re.compile(r'reach(?:ed|es|ing)?$')


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    old_doc, previous = carry if carry is not None else (None, '')
    if doc != old_doc:
        previous = ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1].lower()
    word = token.strip()
    text = previous + token
    boundary = len(previous)
    value = {'each': -0.3, 'reachable': 0.5,
             'unreachable': 0.1, 'outreach': 0.6}.get(word, 0.0)

    if ROOT.fullmatch(word):
        value += 3.6
        if word == 'reaches':
            value -= 0.8
    if 'approach' in token:
        value += 0.4
    if 'stretch' in token:
        value += 0.5
    if 'reich' in token:
        value += 1.2

    internal = (token and previous and token[0].isalpha()
                and previous[-1].isalpha())
    if internal:
        matches = [m for m in RHOTIC.finditer(text)
                   if m.end() > boundary
                   and (m.start() < boundary or len(token) <= 6)]
        ch = [m for m in matches if m[2] == 'ch']
        if ch:
            value += 1.2
        if any(m[2] == 'k' for m in matches):
            value += 0.4
        if any(len(m[1]) >= 2 for m in matches):
            value += 0.4
        if any(m[1] in ('ea', 'ei') for m in ch):
            value += 2.2
        if any(text[:m.start()].endswith('p') for m in ch):
            value += 0.3
        if any(text[:m.start()].endswith('sp') for m in ch):
            value += 3.6
        if re.search(r'r[' + VOWELS + r']{1,3}ch$', previous):
            value += 0.3

        for pattern, strength in ((r'reach', 0.9),
                                  (r'schr', 1.0),
                                  (r'schre', 1.6)):
            if any(m.start() < boundary < m.end()
                   for m in re.finditer(pattern, text)):
                value += strength
        if any(m.end() > boundary and m.start() < boundary + 3
               for m in re.finditer('spr', text)):
            value += 0.9
        if previous.endswith('re'):
            if token.startswith('in'):
                value -= 0.4
            if token.startswith('co'):
                value -= 0.4

    if token == ':' and re.search(r'(?:^|\s)re$', previous):
        value = -2.0
    if (prefix.position >= 2 and token == ':'
            and prefix.token_strings[-2] == 'Title'
            and prefix.token_strings[-3] == '<|endoftext|>'
            and prefix.document_ids[-3] == doc):
        value = 6.6
    return (doc, text[-5:]), value

"""Layer-1 MLP down_proj, component 2110: the "ch" of reach-type words.

The component reads the word being spelled at the current token (lowercase letters,
back to the last space, punctuation or document start) and places it in a family:

  - "spr" + vowel + "ch" (sprach, spricht, sprechen, versprochen): strongest, about 5.3
  - "reach" words (reach, reached, reaching, reproach, cockroach): about 3.8
  - "reich" (reich, reicht, verabreicht, eingereicht): about 3.5
  - any other "r" + vowels + "ch" or "pr" + vowel + "ch" (rechen, brach, gericht, griech):
    weak, about 0.9. "rich" and "approach" are excluded.

The prediction is the family's level on the token where the word first enters that
family (" reach", "spr|icht", "rei|ch"), and 0 on every other token. Only the first
family that matches counts, and a token whose word was already in the same or a
higher family predicts 0.
"""
import re

READS = ()

FAMILIES = [  # (pattern on the word so far, level), first match wins
    (re.compile(r"spr[aeiou]?ch|sprochen"), 5.3),
    (re.compile(r"(?<!fo)(?<![bp])reach|reproach|encroach|cockroach|(?<!p)roach"), 3.8),
    (re.compile(r"reich"), 3.5),
    (re.compile(r"(?<!p)r(?!ich(?!t))[aeiouäöü]+ch|pr[aeio]ch"), 0.9),
]


def _level(word):
    for pattern, level in FAMILIES:
        if pattern.search(word):
            return level
    return 0.0


def _word(prefix, t):
    """Letters of the word ending at token t, lowercase; stops at a document break."""
    doc = prefix.document_ids[t]
    parts = []
    for i in range(t, -1, -1):
        if prefix.document_ids[i] != doc:
            break
        text = prefix.token_strings[i]
        tail = re.search(r"[^\W\d_]*$", text).group(0)
        parts.insert(0, tail.lower())
        if tail != text:
            break
    return "".join(parts)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    now = _level(_word(prefix, t))
    before = _level(_word(prefix, t - 1)) if t > 0 else 0.0
    return carry, float(now if now > before else 0.0)

"""Greek nu (ν) and the closing tool tags.

The component's activation sits mostly on a few tokens. The main one is the Greek
letter ν: its sign and size depend on the vowel letter just before it. After ο (omicron)
it is strongly negative, after ι or η moderately negative, and after υ (upsilon) strongly
positive. Accents and capitals are ignored. The closing tags </tool_call> and
</tool_response> are reliably negative. Everything else is predicted as 0.
"""

import unicodedata

READS = ()

# Activation of ν, by the letter just before it (accents and case removed).
NU_AFTER = {"ο": -6.7, "ι": -3.0, "η": -3.8, "υ": 4.7, "χ": 4.3}
# Activation of the closing tags, by token id.
CLOSING_TAG = {151658: -2.0, 151666: -1.0}  # </tool_call>, </tool_response>


def base_letter(token):
    """The token's letter in lower case, with accents and breathings removed."""
    letters = unicodedata.normalize("NFD", token)
    letters = "".join(c for c in letters if unicodedata.category(c) != "Mn")
    return letters.lower() if len(letters) == 1 else ""


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token in ("ν", "Ν") and len(prefix.token_strings) > 1:
        return carry, NU_AFTER.get(base_letter(prefix.token_strings[-2]), 0.0)
    return carry, CLOSING_TAG.get(prefix.token_ids[-1], 0.0)
